examples.ko: 어떤 대학에 갈지 아직 결정하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I haven't decided yet which university to go to.

examples.ko: 우리 어디서 만날지 지금 같이 결정해요.
examples.en: Let's decide together right now where to meet.
We'll wait. Take your time deciding on the menu.
That person will make the final decision.

examples.ko: 저는 옷을 살 때 뭘 살지 결정하기가 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard for me to decide what to buy when I shop for clothes.
After talking with my parents, I decided to move.

explain: '정하다'가 더 쉽고 일상적이라서 '메뉴를 정해요'처럼 가볍게 말해요. '결정하다'는 고민해서 마지막으로 고를 때 어울려요. '결정을 내리다'라는 말도 자주 써요. 저절로 정해지는 건 '결정되다'예요.
explain_en: '정하다' is easier and more casual ('메뉴를 정해요'); '결정하다' fits a final choice made after some thought. '결정을 내리다' (make a decision) is also very common. When something just gets settled without you choosing, use the passive '결정되다'.

p.n: 정하다 is plainer and more everyday; 결정하다 sounds a bit weightier.

examples.en: My friend is coming to Korea the day after tomorrow.
I haven't studied, and the exam is the day after tomorrow.
Then I'll contact you again around the day after tomorrow.

examples.ko: 오늘은 바빠서 내일모레 만날 수 있어요.
examples.en: I'm busy today, so I can meet the day after tomorrow.
Vacation starts the day after tomorrow, so I'm going on a trip.

examples.ko: 내일모레 여행 가는데 짐을 아직 못 쌌어요.
examples.en: I'm leaving on a trip the day after tomorrow, but I haven't packed yet.

explain: '모레'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰고, 멀지 않은 가까운 앞날을 가리키기도 해요. 그래서 날짜를 정확히 말할 때는 '모레'가 더 분명해요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 나이에 곧 닿는다는 뜻으로, 나이를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about age, meaning someone will reach that age very soon.

explain_en: It means the same as '모레' and can also point to the near future in general. If you want to name the exact day clearly, '모레' is more precise.

examples.en: Sera's birthday party is the evening after tomorrow.

examples.ko: 아이 생일잔치에 친구들을 열 명 초대했어요.
examples.en: We invited ten friends to the child's birthday party.
We decided to hold Grandma's birthday party at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 생일잔치를 집에서 하면 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: If you hold a birthday party at home, there is a lot to prepare.

examples.ko: 어제 생일잔치에서 케이크를 두 조각이나 먹었어요.
examples.en: I ate as many as two pieces of cake at the birthday party yesterday.

examples.ko: 생일잔치 때 입을 옷을 아직 못 골랐어요.
examples.en: I haven't picked out what to wear to the birthday party yet.

explain: '잔치'는 음식을 차리고 여럿이 모이는 자리라서 '생일 파티'보다 조금 전통적인 느낌이 있어요. 젊은 사람들은 보통 '생일 파티'라고 말해요. 같은 식으로 '돌잔치', '환갑잔치'도 써요.
explain_en: '잔치' suggests a gathering with food laid out for many guests, so it feels a bit more traditional than '생일 파티'. Younger people usually say '생일 파티'. The same word appears in '돌잔치' (first birthday feast) and '환갑잔치' (60th birthday feast).

en: to do a part time job; to have a side job; to moonlight

examples.en: I work part-time at a cafe in front of school.
I worked part-time at a convenience store during vacation.
I go to school while working part-time.
The place where I work part-time is close to home.
I'm working part-time at a restaurant every weekend.

examples.ko: 아르바이트해서 모은 돈으로 여행 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'll travel with the money I saved from part-time work.

explain: 일상에서는 줄여서 '알바'라고 많이 말하고, '알바해요', '알바생'처럼 써요. 정규직으로 일하는 건 '일하다'나 '근무하다'라고 해요. '아르바이트를 하다'처럼 풀어서도 자주 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk it is shortened to '알바', as in '알바해요' and '알바생' (part-timer). Full-time work is '일하다' or '근무하다'. You can also split it, as in '아르바이트를 하다'.

examples.ko: 올가을에는 설악산 단풍을 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: This fall I'm going to see the autumn leaves at Seoraksan.
The weather this fall is unusually clear and cool.
Where would be a good family trip destination this fall?
I started taking Korean classes this fall.

examples.ko: 올가을 단풍은 예년만큼 곱지 않다고 해요.
examples.en: They say the autumn leaves this fall aren't as beautiful as usual.

examples.ko: 올가을은 일이 많아서 여행 갈 시간이 없어요.
examples.en: I have so much work this fall that I have no time to travel.

explain: '올해 가을'을 짧게 말한 거예요. 같은 방식으로 '올봄, 올여름, 올겨울'이 있고, 지난해는 '지난가을'처럼 말해요. '이번 가을'도 비슷하게 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a short way of saying 'this year's fall'. The same pattern gives '올봄', '올여름' and '올겨울', and last year's is '지난가을'. '이번 가을' can be used in a similar way.

examples.en: I'm going to study in Korea next year.
My older sister studied in the United States when she was in college.
I want to study abroad, so I'm learning Korean.
I made many friends while studying abroad.
Which country would be good to study in?

examples.ko: 유학한 친구에게 그 나라 이야기를 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard about that country from a friend who studied there.

explain: '한국에 유학하다'보다 '한국으로 유학을 오다', '미국에 유학을 가다'처럼 '가다/오다'와 같이 말하는 일이 더 많아요. 외국에서 공부하는 학생은 '유학생'이에요. 대학에서 한두 학기만 다녀오는 건 '교환 학생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: People more often say '한국으로 유학을 오다' or '미국에 유학을 가다' (with 가다/오다) than 유학하다 alone. A student studying abroad is a '유학생'. Going to a university abroad for just a semester or two is '교환 학생' (exchange student).

examples.en: The theme of this exhibition is autumn.

examples.ko: 테마 파티에 맞는 옷을 입고 갔어요.
examples.en: I went in clothes that fit the theme party.
This cafe has a unique theme.

examples.ko: 먼저 사진 테마를 정하고 나서 장소를 골랐어요.
examples.en: I first decided on the photo theme and then picked the location.
I made several works with the same theme.
I decorated the room to match the theme.

explain: 이야기나 발표의 중심 내용은 '주제'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. 테마는 '테마파크', '테마 여행', '테마 카페'처럼 분위기나 콘셉트를 말하는 합성어에서 잘 나와요. 학교 발표나 토론에서는 '주제'를 써요.
explain_en: For the central idea of a story or presentation, 주제 is far more natural. 테마 appears in compounds about atmosphere or concept, like 테마파크, 테마 여행, and 테마 카페. In school presentations and debates, use 주제.

examples.ko: 선수들이 환호 속에 필드 위로 뛰어나왔어요.
examples.en: The players ran out onto the field amid cheers.

examples.ko: 이 일은 사무실보다 필드에서 배우는 게 많아요.
examples.en: In this job you learn more in the field than in the office.

examples.ko: 골프장은 필드가 넓어서 걷는 시간이 길어요.
examples.en: A golf course is large, so you walk for a long time.

examples.ko: 축구 필드는 길이가 백 미터쯤 돼요.
examples.en: A soccer field is about a hundred meters long.

examples.ko: 저는 필드 경험이 많은 직원을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for staff with a lot of field experience.

examples.ko: 내일은 필드 조사를 하러 시골에 가요.
examples.en: Tomorrow I'm going to the countryside for field research.

explain: 축구장이나 골프장 같은 경기장을 말할 때가 가장 흔해요. 회사에서는 '필드에서 일하다'처럼 사무실 밖 현장을 말하고, 같은 자리에 '현장'도 써요. 학문이나 일의 '분야'를 말할 때는 보통 '분야'를 써요.
explain_en: Its commonest use is for sports grounds like soccer pitches and golf courses. At work, 'working in the field' means outside the office, where '현장' is also used. For a 'field' of study or work, Koreans usually say '분야'.

dis.h: sports ground or golf course; loanword

p.n: 들 means open countryside, so it does not fit a golf course.
